title: Augmentation Hom bijection between two localization models
statement: For a commutative ring A with an ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on its one-object bottom site, a finitely generated ideal I, and two augmented complexes (T,εT),(K,εK) satisfying the ordered localization model predicate [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data] for I, composition with Q(εK) gives a bijection Hom_D(QT,QK)→Hom_D(QT,Q(A[0])). No K-flatness and no map of rings are assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A6R; original node proof step 3, finite localization filtration

proof.text: Let S be the shift-and-isomorphism closure of Q(T) and let P be its right orthogonal. The localized orthogonality theorem says that P contains every degree-zero module on which an element of I acts invertibly. Mathlib makes P a strictly full triangulated subcategory because S is shift stable. Apply the cone filtration theorem to K to put Q(Cone(epsilon_K)) in P. Shift stability also puts its shift by minus one in P. Since Q(T) belongs to S, Hom from Q(T) into either of those cone objects is zero.

The image under Q of the mapping-cone triangle is distinguished. For two maps f,g:Q(T)->Q(K) with equal composites with Q(epsilon_K), apply coyoneda_exact2 to the inverse rotation and to f-g. It factors f-g through the cone shifted by minus one. Its first factor vanishes by Step 1, so f-g=0 and f=g. This proves injectivity.

For g:Q(T)->Q(A[0]), the composite into the cone is zero by Step 1. Apply coyoneda_exact2 to the augmentation triangle to obtain f with g=f composed with Q(epsilon_K). This is surjectivity; pair it with Step 2.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A6R, lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint; the finite-localization orthogonality and cone filtration are split into separate statements; the inverse-rotation and augmentation triangle Hom arguments are complete Lean proofs.

lean.statement:
theorem ringComplex_cech_augmentation_hom_bijective
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)]
    (I : {I : Ideal A // I.FG})
    (T K : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ)
    (εT : T ⟶ ringComplexSingle A) (εK : K ⟶ ringComplexSingle A)
    (hT : RingComplexHasCechModel A I.val T εT)
    (hK : RingComplexHasCechModel A I.val K εK) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun f : DerivedCategory.Q.obj T ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ↦
        f ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map εK)
